when: 2026-08-04, on the branch of this issue at checkpoint 3
what: Criterion 2 and point 3 of the scope: the time between work appearing that a creature standing in the quarters could take, and that creature's first step towards it. The sentence being checked is section 4.1 of the contract — «уход не является работой: он не создаёт job, ничего не резервирует и не мешает сопоставлению — существо на пути к покоям доступно работе на каждом тике».

twoQuantitiesBecauseTheSentenceHasTwoHal.availability: «доступно работе на каждом тике» — on how many of the ticks a jobless ex-combatant spent in the quarters did the matching actually consider it. MatchJobs writes a decision for every creature in its pool — a chosen_* when it hands work out and a diagnostic from RecordWaitingReason when it has none — so a fresh decision of either shape on the tick is the observable form of «сопоставление его видело». Ticks with neither are counted and the reason for each is named from the candidate filter of MatchJobs, read off the snapshot.
twoQuantitiesBecauseTheSentenceHasTwoHal.response: the ticks between a job becoming available to this creature and this creature taking work. A job counts as available while it is unreserved, is not somebody else's personal job, belongs to a kind whose priority is above zero, and its target is reachable from where the creature stands by the map's own BFS. Competition is excluded by construction: a job somebody else reserves stops counting on the tick it is reserved, so a slow answer can never be somebody else's speed.

everyMissedTickNamed.reading: the 563 are creatures with MealReserved, which MatchJobs excludes from its pool by the clause `Mode is not (Eating or ...)` — a rule older than Issue #201 and nothing to do with going off duty. The 3 are the Cause.JobEnded ticks of evidence/228-decomposition.json: the matching had already run when the Rest job finished inside the same tick.

response.firstStepAfterTakingTheJob: max 2 ticks over the whole matrix

theLongOnesAndWhatTheyAre.reading: the four 65-tick runs are all creature #5 on prepared/20260728, on Watch and Drill jobs, and on every one of those ticks it had a meal reserved — the same exclusion as the 563 above. Not one long run over the matrix is a creature that the matching saw, could have given the job to, and did not.

verdictOnTheContract.theSentence: «существо на пути к покоям доступно работе на каждом тике» (docs/design/PROTOTYPE_01_PREPARE_FOR_RAID.md, section 4.1)
verdictOnTheContract.confirmed: as a statement about the off-duty rule, yes, and by measurement rather than by reading the code. Going off duty removes nobody from the matching pool: 84.24 % of jobless quarters ticks were seen by the matching after the rule and 84.94 % before it, and every one of the 566 unseen ticks is a pre-existing exclusion — a reserved meal (563) or the tick a job ended (3). Not one is the walk to the quarters.
verdictOnTheContract.tooStrongAsWritten: «на каждом тике» is literally false and was false before Issue #201 too: on 566 of 3591 ticks the matching did not see the creature. The contract is corrected to say what is measured rather than what is intended.
verdictOnTheContract.andTheResponseIsFast: when work did appear that the creature could take, it took work on the next tick in 31 of 33 cases and after three ticks at worst, and stepped towards it within two ticks of taking it. Whatever holds the group in the quarters, it is not that the matching stopped offering.

whatThisFileDoesNotClaim: that the response sample is large. Thirty-three runs over the matrix, of which four are the creature taking the very job that had been waiting, is a small sample and the mean of 1.09 rests on it. It is enough to rule out a response of tens of ticks, which is what the question needed; it is not enough to distinguish 1.09 from 1.2.
